description: A stately Southern traditional home exterior photographed at dusk from a wide-establishing street view framed by overhanging tree branches. The home is a large two-story white clapboard structure with a classic front porch spanning the full width of the facade. The porch features white turned wooden columns supporting the roof, white wood balustrades along the railing, and painted gray horizontal siding on the base. Wide brick or stone front steps lead up to the porch from a brick paver walkway. Two symmetrical white urn planters flank the base of the steps, each containing a subtropical plant. The front double door is substantial, in rich stained wood with multiple glass panes in a divided light pattern. The roof is standing seam metal in charcoal gray with gabled dormers above. A mature landscaping of azaleas, boxwood, and tropical accent plants lines the front beds. On the porch, visible to the right, a ceiling fan is mounted to the tongue-and-groove painted porch ceiling. Warm amber light glows downward from a centered hanging fixture beneath the porch pediment directly above the front door landing, casting a pool of warmth over the door surround and upper steps. The sky above is a deep gray-blue dusk tone. The overall palette is white, charcoal, warm wood, and rich green. Camera is at a standing eye-level, centered symmetrical wide establishing view from across the front lawn, looking straight at the house with the porch framed between trees.
